newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Northam strike could hasten Rusplats merger.
newsitem.headline: Northam strike could hasten Rusplats merger.

text.p: A strike by unionised workers at South Africa's troubled Northam Platinum Ltd mine could hasten a merger with neighbouring Rustenburg Platinum Mines Ltd, analysts said.
The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Wednesday 96.8 percent of its 3,300 members at Northam had voted in favour of strike action over wages.
Management at the mine, which produced 75,365 ounces of precious metal in concentrates in the three months to September, reached deadlock in talks with the union last month.

Northam owners Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said at its results presentation this week that violent conflict between Zulu and Xhosa workers at Northam during August had resulted in the loss of 50,000 tonnes of ore.
Analysts said other platinum producers in South Africa could weather such a loss without a massive impact on earnings.
But Northam, which slipped back into loss in the September quarter after a maiden profit in the previous three months, was ill-equipped to weather disruptions.

"If the strike goes ahead, they get themselves into pretty serious problems," BOE Natwest platinum analyst Paul Brogan said, adding that Northam may reverse its previous practice of not retrenching and sack all 3,300 NUM members.
Brogan said among the possible options Gold Fields may consider was a merger with the Amandelbult section of Rustenburg, owned by Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd.
The Amandelbult section of Rustenburg lies adjacent to Northam and Amplats said last June that it was interested in the neighbouring operation.
Analysts said Northam would be in serious trouble if a strike was called this week, because it had only about 25 million rand in cash reserves.

"They could close the mine, they could talk to their neighbours or they could borrow the money to get themeselves through the bad times," said a Johannesburg platinum analyst who asked not to be named.
Brogan said he believed the mine would not be able to weather a strike beyond a few days.
"They (Northam) haven't got the ability to weather it beyond a couple of days...That is why the issue of a merger with Rusplats becomes even more urgent".
Analysts said Northam's plunge into the red in the September quarter showed the mine's vulnerability to factors other South African platinum producers could shrug off.

"Northam is very sensitive to production, and to exchange rate and to prices and this last quarter's results just goes to prove that this loss of production in August can just tip the balance from profit into loss," Brogan said.
